rationale: fastdiff_wdm_wavelet_unconstrained-claude-agentic: val_n=200, seed=42, fd_recon_steps=8, fd_recon_init=fbp, fd_recon_init_t=0.2, fd_recon_eta=1.0, fd_recon_dc=1, fd_recon_dc_n_cg=5, fd_recon_dc_relax=1.0, dataset_kind=breast_ct, rationale=iter-4 PRIOR-INFLUENCE lever continued (fd_recon_init_t 0.4->0.2), fastdiff_wdm_wavelet_unconstrained breast val=200. SIX-BOX: (1) PRIOR: MONOTONE trend as prior influence drops: iter-1(t0.7,relax0.5) SSIM0.712/PSNR27.04; iter-2(relax1.0) 0.814/27.49; iter-3(t0.4) 0.894/27.87 -- all hr=0, all ~8.5+ dB below the 128-view sparse-FBP floor (PSNR36.32/RMSE0.0052). (2) Failure mode: the mis-scaled MAYO wavelet prior (out_scale0.05 vs breast mu0.5) is purely HARMFUL; every knob that reduces its trajectory influence improves the recon, but with diminishing PSNR returns (+0.44, +0.38 dB). (3) ONE KNOB: fd_recon_init_t 0.4->0.2 (even stronger FBP anchor, near-minimal prior), else = iter-3. (4) HYPOTHESIS: if the monotone 'less-prior-is-better' trend holds, SSIM/PSNR rise again toward (but likely still below) the FBP floor, confirming the Mayo wavelet prior adds NOTHING on sparse breast; init_t->0 is the pure-FBP+CG limit. This isolates whether ANY prior weight helps (it appears not). If PSNR plateaus/regresses, we've found the best usable init_t and pivot to fd_recon_steps (iter-5). (5) BUDGET: free knob. (6) Loop continues; iter-5 on landing.
